en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Training Rules (Sekhiyakanda)
Ujjagghikavagga 18.
The Second Training Rule on Swinging the Arms.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks sat in inhabited areas swinging their arms and letting them hang down...
[as before] ... "The training is to be observed: 'I shall not sit in an inhabited area swinging my arms.
One must not sit in an inhabited area swinging one's arms."
One should sit with one’s arm held up.
Whoever, out of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area swinging his arms or letting his arm hang down, commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense—
unintentionally,
through lack of mindfulness,
or not knowing;
For one who is ill,
for one who has entered upon the rains retreat,
and in times of distress.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of the first offender.
The eighth training rule is concluded.
